verdict.rationale: DBOS's queue system provides 'managed concurrency' and flow control for running many workflows across a program (dbos-docs-6), and workflows/steps are checkpointed to Postgres so any worker crash leaves state recoverable and workflows can restart from where they left off (dbos-docs-3, dbos-docs-4). A competitor's technical critique (dbos-comm-6) confirms DBOS actually implements a Postgres 'FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' pattern for distributing queued tasks among workers, which is the underlying mechanism that would let multiple worker processes pull tasks and load-balance without a central dispatcher, and worker/service crash tolerance is repeatedly emphasized (dbos-docs-11, dbos-comm-13, dbos-comm-14). However, there is no first-party documentation or benchmark that explicitly frames 'add workers → throughput scales linearly' or describes fleet-wide load-balancing guarantees, and one community note (dbos-comm-7) raises operational caveats about locking/lock contention at scale. Missing for 10: an explicit docs page/benchmark on horizontal worker scaling and throughput, and independent verification of load-balancing behavior under real multi-worker fleets.
